column2: One who breaks vows and one who has fallen from his own stage of life: both fall into the middle of the torment called Sandamsha.
Men who are celibate students but emit semen in dreams by day, and those who are taught by their sons, fall into Shvabhojana.
These and other hells number hundreds and thousands, in which evildoers undergoing torment are cooked.
Likewise these sins and thousands of others are suffered by the persons of each class who range in the various hells.
Men who do actions contrary to their varna and ashrama, by deed, mind or speech, fall into the hells.
Denizens of hell are seen by the gods in heaven with heads downward, and the gods see all the denizens of hell face-down below.
Plants, worms, goats (?), birds, beasts, men, the righteous, gods and the liberated are, in order, each a thousandth part (of the one before).
The second is in succession a thousandth of the first; all of these are fortunate until they take refuge in liberation.
As many creatures as are in heaven, so many dwell in hell. The sinner who turns away from expiation goes to hell.
Expiations fitting each sin have been stated by the great sages, recalling them as they should be.
For grave sins heavy, and for light sins light, expiations were sung by Svayambhuva and others, best of Brahmins, who knew them.
Of all the expiations consisting of austerity and rites, the supreme of them all is remembrance of Krishna.
For the man who feels remorse after sin, the one supreme expiation is remembrance of Hari.
Remembering Narayana in the morning, at night, at twilights, at midday and the like, a man at once attains destruction of sin.
By remembering Vishnu, with the whole mass of afflictions destroyed, one attains liberation, Brahmins, by praising that Vishnu.
Whose mind is on Vasudeva in chanting, offering, worship and the like — for him the obstacle is, best of Brahmins, only the fruit such as Indra-hood.
How can there be a going to heaven, marked by return, compared with chanting "Vasudeva", the supreme seed of liberation?
Therefore the twice-born man who constantly remembers Vishnu day and night does not go to hell; he is pure, all his sins destroyed.
Heaven is what pleases the mind, hell is its opposite; merit and sin are called heaven and hell, best of Brahmins.
Since one and the same thing may cause sorrow, pleasure, the rise of envy and anger, how can a thing be of the nature of sorrow?
The same thing, having been for pleasure, becomes again for sorrow; the same, for one who is angry, becomes for satisfaction.
Therefore nothing is of the nature of sorrow and nothing of the nature of pleasure; this is a transformation of the mind marked by pleasure, pain and the like.
Knowledge alone is the supreme Brahman; ignorance is held to be for bondage. This universe is of the nature of knowledge; there is nothing beyond knowledge.
Knowledge and ignorance, Brahmins — let only knowledge be ascertained. Thus this circle of the earth has been told to you by me,
and all the nether worlds and the hells, Brahmins, oceans, mountains, continents, varshas and rivers; all has been told in brief. What more do you wish to hear?
A full hundred thousand yojanas above the moon, the entire circle of the constellations shines above.
Two hundred thousand (yojanas) further up, Brahmins, is Mercury above the circle of the constellations; at an equal distance above Mercury is Venus.
Mars also stands at that same distance above Venus; at two hundred thousand above Mars stands the priest of the gods (Jupiter).
Saturn is established two hundred thousand above Jupiter; from there, one hundred thousand above, best of Brahmins, is the circle of the Seven Sages.
Above the sages by a hundred thousand is Dhruva established, as the pivot of the whole circle of luminaries.
This triple world has been told in brief, best of Brahmins; this earth is the field of the fruit of sacrifice, and sacrifice is established here.
Above Dhruva is Maharloka, where the dwellers for a kalpa live; Maharloka is ordained as one crore yojanas.
Janaloka is two crores, where Brahma's sons, Sanandana and the others, pure-minded, are said to dwell, Brahmins.
Above Janaloka, four times as far, is Tapas, where the Vairaja gods dwell, bodiless.
Six times beyond Tapoloka shines Satyaloka, from which there is no return, served by Siddhas and sages.
Whatever object reachable on foot is made of earth is called Bhurloka; its extent has been told by me.
The region between the earth and the sun, served by Siddhas and sages, is called Bhuvarloka, the second, best of sages.
The region between Dhruva and the sun, fourteen niyutas, is called Svarloka by those who ponder the world's arrangement.
This triple world is recited by the Brahmins as made (kritaka); Jana, Tapas and Satya are the unmade three.
Maharloka in the middle is remembered as both made and unmade; it becomes empty at the kalpa's end but does not perish.
These seven great worlds have been told by me, Brahmins, and seven nether worlds: this is the extent of the Brahmanda.
This egg is enveloped all around — across, above and below — by the egg-shell, as the seed of the kapittha fruit is by its rind.
The egg is surrounded by water ten times (its size); that water is surrounded outside by fire;
fire by wind, wind by space, Brahmins; space too, best of sages, is surrounded by the Mahat.
All these seven, each ten times the last, enclose Mahat, and Pradhana stands encompassing it.
There is no end or count of that Infinite; it is infinite and uncounted even by measure.
That Prakriti, the supreme, is the cause of all, Brahmins; of eggs there are thousands of thousands and tens of thousands,
and hundreds of crores of crores of such there. As fire is in wood and oil in sesame, so the Purusha is here.
Established in Pradhana, pervading, the Purusha is self-awareness; Pradhana and Purusha, both,
are held by Vishnu's power, which is felt in all beings, best of Brahmins; they depend on each other. That same power is the cause of their separation and of dependence,
and the cause of agitation at the time of creation, best of Brahmins. As wind carries coolness in water as droplets,
so Vishnu's world-power consists of Pradhana and Purusha. As a tree with root, trunk, branches and the like
arises from an original seed, then other seeds come from it, and from those other trees arise,
these too following the cause, substances with the same marks, Brahmins — so from the Unmanifest first arise Mahat and the rest,
ending with the specific; from them arise gods and others, from them sons, and from their sons further sons.
As there is no loss to the tree by the sprouting of a tree from the seed, so there is no loss to the elements by the creation of beings.
As by mere proximity space, time and the rest are the cause of the tree, so the Lord Hari, without transformation, is the cause of the universe.
As in a rice seed there are root, stalk, leaf, shoot, joint, sheath, flower, milk and grain,
husks and grains, which come into manifestation of themselves on obtaining the complete causes of sprouting, best of sages,
so in many actions the bodies of gods and others stand, and, obtaining Vishnu's power, they come to sprouting.
And that Vishnu is the Supreme Brahman, from whom is all this world, who is the world, and in whom this will dissolve.
That Brahman is the supreme abode, the being and non-being, the highest state; whose, without distinction, is this entire world of moving and unmoving.
He alone is the root nature, the manifest form, and the world; in him alone all dissolves and in him all stays.
He is the doer of acts, he is worshipped as the sacrifice, he is the fruit of that action; whatever begins with the yuga and comes to be entirely — nothing is other than Hari.
Having gathered the water of the heavenly Ganga, the lord of rays at once showers it on the earth with his rays, even from a cloudless sky.
A mortal whose mud of sin is shaken off by its touch, best of Brahmins, does not go to hell; that is remembered as divine bathing.
That water seen by the sun falls from the sky without clouds; the heavenly Ganga water is cast by the sun's rays.
The water that falls from the sky in odd-numbered stars such as Krittika, seen with the sun, should be known as Ganga water, thrown by the elephants of the directions.
The water that falls from the sky in the even-numbered stars, drawn by the sun, is quickly gathered and expelled by the sun's rays.
Both are exceedingly holy, removers of men's sin, Brahmins; the heavenly Ganga water is divine bathing, best of Brahmins.
The water released by clouds nourishes beings, Brahmins; all plants, for it is the nectar for life.
By it the entire mass of herbs is brought to great growth, and what is required, up to the ripening of fruit, is produced for people.
By it humans with the eye of scripture perform sacrifices as prescribed, and every day they gratify the gods.
Thus sacrifices, Vedas, the varnas headed by Brahmins, all hosts of gods, and the herds of beasts and creatures
— this whole world, moving and unmoving, is sustained by rain; and that rain is brought about by the Sun, best of sages.
The support of the Sun, best of sages, is Dhruva; the Dhruva's is the Shishumara (Dolphin) constellation, and it too rests on Narayana.
In the heart of that Shishumara stands Narayana, the supporter of all beings, primeval, eternal.
Thus the Brahmanda with earth, oceans and the rest has been told by me, best of sages. What else do you wish to hear?
the golden well, the Shveta-tirtha lake, the pool of Gharghari, Shyamakupa, Chandrika,

Ishutirtha, Varshabha, Kaverihrada, Kanyatirtha, Gokarna, Gayatri-sthana,

Sarvadevavrata, Kanyashramahrada, another of the Valakhilyas, with earlier ones, and another,
and another of the great sages, Akhanditahrada; at these tirthas, by rule, properly, with faith,
the mortal who bathes, fasting, with senses controlled, having satisfied gods, sages, humans and ancestors in order,
and worshipped the deities, and stayed three nights — in each of these tirthas separately, Brahmins,
obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice; no doubt here. One who constantly hears this excellent glory of the tirthas, or reads or makes it heard, is freed from all sins.
Kashyapa, Jamadagni, Bharadvaja, Gautama, Vasishtha, Jaimini, Dhaumya, Markandeya, Valmiki,
Vishvamitra, Shatananda, Vatsya, Gargya, Asuri, Sumantu, Bhargava, Kanva, Medhatithi, Guru,

Narada, Parvata, Vaishampayana, Galava, Bhaskari, Purana, Suta, Pulastya, Kapila,
Uluka, Pulaha, Vayu, Devasthana, Chaturbhuja, Sanatkumara, Paila, Krishna, Krishnanubhautika:
surrounded by these and other best of sages, the son of Satyavati, the glorious sage, shone like the moon among stars.
The Veda-knower honoured all those sages who came, and they too, honouring him in return, conversed among themselves.
At the end of the conversation those best of sages, dwellers of the austerity forest, all asked Krishna, Satyavati's son, a doubt:

Sage, you know the Vedas and sciences, Puranas, Agamas and the Bharata, past, future and present, all literature.
brahmapuran:26:19	In this painful ocean of existence, full of sorrow, without essence, crowded with crocodiles of attachment, terrible, flooded by the waters of the senses' objects,
brahmapuran:26:20	with whirlpools of the senses' mud, thick with hundreds of seen waves, muddy with the mire of delusion, difficult, deep and hard to cross because of greed,
brahmapuran:26:21	seeing the world sinking, unsupported, unconscious, we ask you, fortunate one; tell us, best of sages:
brahmapuran:26:22	what is best in this terrible, hair-raising worldly existence? You ought to lift up the worlds by giving instruction.
brahmapuran:26:23	You ought to tell us of the rare supreme holy place that gives liberation, and we wish to hear of the land of action on earth.
brahmapuran:26:24	A man who properly does action on earth as prescribed attains supreme success, and hell by wrong action;
brahmapuran:26:25	and in a field of liberation the wise man attains liberation. Therefore tell, greatly wise one, what you are asked, best of Brahmins.
Hearing the words of those sages of purified minds, the revered Vyasa, knower of past, future and present, said:

Listen, all you sages; I shall tell, since you ask, the dialogue that took place formerly between the sages and Brahma.
brahmapuran:26:28	On the broad back of Meru, adorned with many jewels, strewn with many trees and creepers, graced with many flowers,
brahmapuran:26:29	lovely with the cries of many birds, crowded with many springs, filled with many creatures, endowed with many wonders,
brahmapuran:26:30	strewn with rocks of many colours, adorned with many minerals, crowded with many sages, furnished with many hermitages —
brahmapuran:26:31	there was seated the Lord of the world, source of the world, four-faced, master of the world, worshipped by the world, support of the world, the Lord,
brahmapuran:26:32	surrounded by gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Vidyadharas, serpents, sages, Siddhas, Apsarases and other dwellers of heaven.
brahmapuran:26:33	Some praised that god, some sang before him, some played instruments, and others danced.
brahmapuran:26:34	At such a joyful time, at the gathering of all beings, rich with the fragrance of many flowers, served by the southern breeze,
brahmapuran:26:35	Bhrigu and the others then bowed to the god, the Grandfather, and the best of sages, Brahmins, asked their father this matter:
brahmapuran:26:36	'Revered one, we wish to hear of the land of action on earth; you ought to tell, lord of gods, of the rare field of liberation.'
brahmapuran:26:37	Hearing their words, Brahma, lord of the gods, said — as they had asked the question — all that, best of sages.

Therefore, Brahma, tell us of Bharata in detail, if you have compassion on us, and as it stands.
brahmapuran:27:13	Lord, tell us fully of this varsha, of its mountains and the divisions of this varsha.

Hear of the Bharata varsha, Brahmins, of nine divisions; they should be known as separated by sea and mutually inaccessible:
brahmapuran:27:15	Indradvipa, Kaseru, Tamravarna, Gabhastiman, Nagadvipa, Saumya, Gandharva and Varuna,
brahmapuran:27:16	and this ninth of them, a continent surrounded by the ocean, a thousand yojanas from south to north.
brahmapuran:27:17	In its east are Kiratas, in the west Yavanas; Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras are stationed in the middle.
brahmapuran:27:18	Purified by actions such as sacrifice, war and trade, their dealings are carried on by these actions;
brahmapuran:27:19	and merit and sin are the causes of heaven and liberation. Mahendra, Malaya, Sahya, Shuktiman, Riksha,
brahmapuran:27:20	Vindhya and Pariyatra: these seven are the family mountains here; of them there are thousands of other mountains nearby,
brahmapuran:27:21	broad and high, lovely, with varied slopes: Kolahala, Vaibhraja, Mandara, Dardala,
brahmapuran:27:22	Vatamdhaya, Vaidyuta, Mainaka, Surasa, Tungaprastha, Nagagiri, Godhana, Pandara,
brahmapuran:27:23	Pushpagiri, Vaijayanta, Raivata, Arbuda, Rishyamuka, Gomantha, Kritashaila, Kritachala,
brahmapuran:27:24	Shriparvata, Chakora and hundreds of other mountains. Mixed with them are countries, and Mlecchas and others in portions.
brahmapuran:27:25	By them the best of rivers are drunk; understand them, best of Brahmins: Ganga, Sarasvati, Sindhu, Chandrabhaga and another,
brahmapuran:27:26	Yamuna, Shatadru, Vipasha, Vitasta, Airavati, Kuhu, Gomati, Dhutapapa, Bahuda, Drishadvati,
brahmapuran:27:27	Vipasha, Devika, Chakshu, Nishthivi, Gandaki, Kaushiki, Apaga: those issuing from the foot of the Himalaya.
brahmapuran:27:28	Devasmriti, Devavati, Vataghni, Sindhu, Veni, Chandana, Sadanira, Mahi,
brahmapuran:27:29	Charmanvati, Vrishi, Vidisha, Vedavati, Sipra and Avanti are remembered as following Pariyatra.
brahmapuran:27:30	Shona, the great river Narmada, Surathā, Kriya, Mandakini, Dasharna and another, Chitrakuta,
brahmapuran:27:31	Chitrotpala, Vetravati, Karamoda, Pishachika, another, Atilaghushroni, Vipapma and the river Shaivala.
